svg.text: Podular Service – Pod Removal by Forklift
Pod removal – hinged deck lid, safety zone and forklift lift
BASE FRAME AND LOCKING PINS STAY ON DECK
DRIVE SHAFT PARTED AT DISCONNECT PIN
VERTICAL SHAFT AND BLADE UNIT BELOW
Set out the safety zone – temporary bollards into the deck sockets, tape off.
Isolate at the switchgear shed, lock off and confirm dead.
Release the lid catches; flip the deck lid outboard on its hinges.
Part the vertical drive shaft at the disconnect pin below the deck.
Withdraw the 4 no. locking pins from the pod base frame.
Hook the 4-leg chain set to the lifting eyes; lift clear with the forklift.
Lower onto the trailer; small truck to the service yard.
Reverse for the serviced pod: re-pin, re-couple, close the lid, test.
is drawn out and the two
Pins are withdrawn by hand from the deck.
No bolts to undo and no diver required.
INDICATIVE ARTIST'S ILLUSTRATION – NOT TO SCALE
Dimensions to be confirmed by survey and detailed design
The deck around each pod is timber on hinges. The lid flips outboard, opening the shaft and the blade unit below without any cutting or hot work.
Sockets cast into the deck take temporary bollards. Bollards and tape set out an OH&S compliant safety zone before any lid is opened.
A generic forklift with a jib and 4-leg chain set engages the four lifting eyes on the pod roof — see Drawing 3.
4 no. locking pins are withdrawn from the base frame and the vertical drive shaft is parted at its disconnect pin before the pod is lifted.
The pod is lowered onto a trailer, or laid on the deck, and taken by small truck to the service yard. A serviced pod is swapped straight back in.
No diver, no crane barge and no shutdown of the neighbouring units are required. Target service interval 6 months.
